title: How do you verify the business behind an AI agent?
summary: Learn how to verify the business behind an AI agent by identifying the operating enterprise, verifying authorized representatives, and managing delegated authority.
body_markdown:
Autonomous programs execute tasks by issuing API calls, negotiating orders, and transferring funds across business networks. Counterparties cannot rely on software identity alone to collect debts or enforce contractual terms. Every commercial interaction must tie back to an identifiable commercial enterprise formed and operating under state corporate law.


Verifying that entity starts with corporate formation and registration records. Counterparties confirm that the business maintains an active charter with its home state filing office, such as a[Secretary of State](https://www.sos.state.co.us/) registry, and verify its federal Employer Identification Number (EIN). These checks demonstrate that the company is a recognized corporate entity in good standing rather than an unregistered shell or dissolved business.


Corporate existence alone does not prove that the person deploying the agent has the legal right to bind the company. A complete verification workflow identifies the human representative directing the deployment and confirms their role through corporate filings or commercial signing records. Under foundational[agency law principles](https://www.law.cornell.edu/wex/agency) , a commercial enterprise is bound when an agent acts with actual or apparent authority granted by the principal. Establishing who authorized the system creates an unbroken chain of legal accountability from the running code back to corporate leadership.
